51275109.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant human full-length HSP90alpha by surface plasmon resonance analysis
51275109.references_previous: Reference 32: Wang, L.; Li, L.; Gu, K.; Xu, X.; Sun, Y.; You, Q.-D. Targeting Hsp90-Cdc37: a promising therapeutic strategy by inhibiting Hsp90 chaperone function. Curr. Drug Targets 2017, 18, 1572–1585.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Bioluminescence Resonance Energy Transfer (BRET) Assay. The BRET assay was performed as described previously.32 Briefly, the Hsp90-Cdc37 complex was formed by co-transfecting HEK293T cells with pCMV-Tag2B-Hsp90α (donor) and pCMV-Tag2B-Cdc37 (acceptor) plasmids. After 48 h, cells were lysed and the BRET signal was measured using a Synergy H1 Multi-Mode Microplate Reader (BioTek). The BRET ratio was calculated as the ratio of emission at 610 nm to that at 480 nm. The BRET ratio of the Hsp90-Cdc37 complex in the presence of compounds was normalized to that of the control (DMSO).
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. 18h directly bound to Hsp90. (A) Binding affinity of 18h with Hsp90 protein, determined by binding kinetic assay of biolayer interferometry (ForteBio Octet). The K_D value was 0.5 μM. (B) Direct binding experiments of Hsp90 and 18h, determined by binding thermodynamic assay of ITC. The K_d value was 0.63 μM. (C) 1H STD NMR spectrum of 100 μM 18h binding to 5 μM Hsp90. ppm, parts per million. All data are representative of three independent experiments.
